title: Consolidate consumer error handling and adaptive throttling for queue workers
creator: Aisha Kaur
description:
Background: Over the last year weve accumulated a number of ad-hoc consumer behaviors across different async pipelines (Redis stream workers, Kafka consumers, and internal async job runners). Each subsystem implements slightly different retry backoff, DLQ placement, and throttling semantics which makes incident response and capacity planning difficult. This ticket consolidates error handling into a small shared library, introduces an adaptive throttling controller, and standardizes DLQ semantics so that we can reduce duplicated code and improve SLO adherence.

Goals: 1) Implement a shared consumer error handling library used by Redis and Kafka consumers that unifies retry windows, jitter, and DLQ routing. 2) Add an adaptive throttling controller that responds to downstream pressure (SLO violations, CPU/GPU saturation, queue lag) and can push back at producer/ingestor-level via leaky-bucket tokens or by toggling consumer concurrency. 3) Ensure safe migration with feature flags and gradual rollout. 4) Ship observability (metrics, tracing, dashboard) and test harnesses for chaos testing and load tests.
acceptance_criteria: Shared error-handling library published (internal npm/py artifact) and consumed by at least two worker types
Retry policy standardized: exponential backoff with configurable max attempts and randomized jitter; default max attempts = 5
DLQ semantics defined and implemented: deterministic DLQ topics/streams with envelope metadata for replay
Adaptive throttling controller prototype deployed to staging reacting to simulated downstream saturation
No regression in end-to-end latency SLOs; <1% increase in 95th latency observed in controlled canary
Automated integration test simulates consumer node crash and validates exactly-once (or at-least-once documented) behavior and DLQ placement
Documentation (confluence) outlining upgrade steps and rollback plan
technical_notes: Library API: consume(message) -> returns ACK | NACK_RETRY | NACK_DLQ; includes attachable context for tracing and tenant id
Retry semantics: base = 200ms, multiplier = 2, max_backoff = 30s, jitter = 0.2*value; configurable per queue via configstore
DLQ format: {original_topic, partition, offset, attempts, cause, timestamp, trace_id} to enable replay and debugging
Redis workers use XGROUP ACK/NACK semantics; implement a centralized pending-id checkpointing to reduce duplication
Kafka consumers leverage a small compensating service for delayed retries (retry topics with TTL) to avoid blocking primary partitions
Adaptive throttling: controller samples consumer lag, CPU/GPU queue length, request failure rate; outputs target concurrency and token-bucket refill rate
Compatibility: provide shim for legacy consumer code path to opt-in via feature flag; gradual migration expected
migration_plan: 1) Publish v0.1 of error-handling library to internal package registry and add to khan/redis-worker and phoenix/kafka-consumer in feature branches
2) Run integration tests in staging with synthetic workload replay; validate DLQ format and retry counts
3) Enable library behind feature flag on small subset of workers (~5% of traffic) and monitor metrics for 48h
4) Incrementally increase to 25% then 100% providing rollback toggles remain available
5) Turn on adaptive throttling controller in read-only mode in production to collect signals for 2 weeks, then enable active throttling in canary region
6) Deprecate legacy retry helpers and remove duplicate implementations after 1 release cycle
rollout_steps: Create feature flag 'consumer_shared_error_handling' in FF service
Deploy library to worker images and start with feature off
Enable flag for staging and run full integration suite
Canary enable for low-traffic service routes for 48h
Monitor dashboards and error budgets, then increase traffic in phases
Activate adaptive throttling controller in canary and observe automatic concurrency adjustments
Full enable and post-mortem checklist completed
test_plan: Unit tests for backoff calculation and jitter distribution
Integration tests: end-to-end message lifecycle including DLQ writing and replay
Load test: 10k msg/s sustained in staging to validate controller behavior
Chaos test: kill consumer pods randomly to ensure idempotency and safe replay
SLO regression test comparing baseline and patched pipeline under identical workload
monitoring_metrics: incident_alerts triggered by queue_lag > threshold for >5m
comments: 2025-01-13 Marco Chen: Did an initial audit of consumer implementations across services. Found 7 distinct retry implementations and 4 different DLQ formats. Plan: consolidate to 1 library and two adapters.
2025-01-20 Aisha Kaur: Reviewed prototype API; requested explicit trace propagation and tenant metadata added to DLQ envelope. Also asked for a small compatibility shim for legacy workers.

2025-01-28 Diego Morales: Implemented adaptive throttling controller prototype. Controller supports policy plugins and currently exposes token-bucket and concurrency controls. Need to harden decision logic under noisy signals.
2025-02-02 QA Automation: Staging integration tests passed for redis-worker feature branch at low load. Observed 2% higher p95 due to added envelope serialization — optimizing serializer next.
2025-02-05 Marco Chen: Enabled feature flag for canary group (~5% traffic) in us-west-2. Monitoring looks healthy; no DLQ spike. Next step: increase to 25% and run load test.
